record.tranche_reason: This is the original study. It trains synthetic-feature toy networks and measures whether features are represented in superposition, how sparsity and importance affect the result, and what geometries form.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own toy-model experiments and explicit reported outcomes. Observations about real models and replications in the comments are not rows because they are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is the original source of the claim (arXiv:2209.10652). It trains ReLU toy networks on synthetic sparse features and directly measures superposition, phase changes, geometry and neuron polysemanticity. Because it is the original, it gets no verdict labels.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, with two additions. The authors demonstrate superposition in toy ReLU networks, governed by sparsity and importance through phase changes, with polytope geometry, coexisting mono- and polysemantic neurons, and computation (absolute value) in superposition. They hypothesize that real networks noisily simulate larger sparse networks. They expect superposition and polysemanticity to generalize, but consider the geometry and learning-dynamics results much more uncertain.
record.recipe_differences: This is the original toy-model study: synthetic sparse feature vectors, learned projection/reconstruction weights, and ReLU variants. No comparison to a separate original method applies.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature sparsity and relative importance alter which features are represented and their geometry; feature correlations also alter their arrangement. The displayed ReLU hidden-layer solutions were selected as lowest-loss results from 1000 training runs.

fits_no_version.finding: Vulnerability to analytic L2 adversarial attacks rises sharply (>3x) as superposition forms and tracks features per dimension. Adversarial training reduces superposition but needs attacks at 80% of input L2 norm to eliminate it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition in toy models is linked to adversarial vulnerability.

fits_no_version.finding: During training, features jump discretely between dimensionality levels, coinciding with sudden loss drops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition geometry emerges through discrete energy-level-like jumps during training.

record.problems: Evidence is from synthetic toy networks, not real models. The authors state that some geometric results may be idiosyncratic to the toy model and that generalization is unclear. Several results are qualitative; the displayed ReLU hidden-layer examples were selected from 1000 runs, and uncertainty estimates are not given.
record.rows_left_out: External replications and follow-up findings in the comments were excluded because they are not this study's own results. Observations about polysemantic neurons in InceptionV1 and Transformer MLPs are not new measurements in this paper. Adversarial-example vulnerability results were omitted because the listed versions do not concern adversarial robustness.

untested.parts: Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure is not tested.
No new measurements in LLMs or with SAEs. InceptionV1 and Transformer MLP polysemanticity is cited from the authors' experience only.
Whether dictionary features are complete, stable or canonical is not tested.
Features are assumed to be 1-D directions by construction. Multi-dimensional features are only discussed in an appendix, which is absent from this text.

missing.what: Learning-dynamics results: discrete feature-dimensionality jumps, and a geometric-transformation sequence for n=6, m=3 with correlated sets. These bear on V1 geometry and its formation.
missing.locator: Superposition and Learning Dynamics — Phenomenon 1 and 2

missing.what: Authors' own follow-up (Henighan & Olah comment): cleaner polytope structure with more features competing and longer training.
Empirical observation that per-feature dimensionalities sum to roughly m when features are efficiently packed.
missing.locator: The Geometry of Superposition — Feature Dimensionality

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are given because this study is the original source of the claim. The V1 and V2 rows are otherwise sound. The replications by external researchers in the comments are correctly excluded as rows; they could be recorded as separate studies.

versions.untested_parts: No test in real models; toy-model computation in superposition is demonstrated only for absolute value.
No test that this explains polysemanticity in real networks or that capacity is the only cause.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
No new measurements in LLMs or SAE feature recovery; real-model observations and follow-up work are discussed or cited.
The study does not test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The experiments use feature vectors/directions; they do not compare one-dimensional features against multidimensional feature representations or establish the claim for real models.
